domain: Whether the concept of 'sportsmanship' can survive the professionalization of officiating technology (VAR, Hawk-Eye, goal-line sensors) in elite sport
topic: Whether the concept of 'sportsmanship' can survive the professionalization of officiating technology (VAR, Hawk-Eye, goal-line sensors) in elite sport

movement.gist: Defend the thesis that officiating technology has made sport meaningfully more just — fewer wrongly disallowed goals, wrongly awarded penalties, wrongly declared boundaries; the old romantic complaints about 'the human element' are mostly nostalgia for injustice we happened to like.

Land the objection: precision has not reduced controversy, it has relocated it — into contested millimetre offside lines, frame-rate ambiguity, and endless deliberation that drains the very drama sportsmanship depended on (the handshake, the accepted bad call, the shared shrug).

primary.axis: justice of outcome vs. legitimacy of the contest as a human moral drama
poles: correctness is not the same good that sportsmanship was ever protecting
fairness as accuracy of the call
fairness as the shared human fallibility both sides submit to

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension is what the frame shift exposes: the debate about cameras and sensors was never really about correctness, it was a debate about which vocabulary of fairness we are willing to keep speaking in

family_realization.note: Passage executes 'Costed Victory' flawlessly. Thesis (tech = just) defended in ¶1-2; final movement (¶3-4) tallies concessions: assent lost. Simultaneous triumph and loss embedded in 'verdict stands' + 'price is exact.' Tone sustains both.

ending_behavior.note: 'The Practical Deflation' perfected: grand movement (two fairnesses, institutional choice) lands on tiny image—'arms folded, waiting to be told what they saw.' Aperture narrows precisely. Resolution costed, not resolved.

voice_consistency.note: 'Recovering Enthusiast' held throughout. 'I was right, which still surprises me' + 'I still defend that' sustain warmth under critique. Minor drift toward essay-register in ¶3's theoretical density, but recovers via concrete handshake imagery.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(A): half_truth trap—plausible but stops short of deeper claim. Q2(B): framework_import—addresses accuracy author grants, not assent loss. Q3(A): phrase_misuse—literal money reading. Q4(C): scope_inflation. Q5(B): prior_belief. Q6(A/C): framework_import + false_symmetry. Traps are genuine, not lexical extremity.

explanation_quality.note: Every wrong option tied to specific passage mechanics: half_truth names paragraph isolation, framework_import names local-claim overgeneration, false_symmetry names the ¶3 distinction collapse, phrase_misuse names literal/metaphor confusion. Zero 'not mentioned' filler.

answers.reasoning: Passage's core turn: accuracy gained, shared assent to finality lost.
Rising disputes despite accuracy directly shows assent was lost, not correctness.
Author literally defines assent as mutual willingness to accept outcomes as final.
Genuine reconciliation regardless of outcome contradicts claim handshake is mere choreography.
Establishes prior belief so later nuanced revision gains rhetorical force.
He defends justice gained but mourns loss of shared finality/assent.
